messages.subject: irace issue with parallel cores
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm having a hard time running EDA in parallel on a university server. When I tried to use 10, 16, and 3 cores (by setting parallel to N in scenario.txt), I got the following error (repeated several times):

Error : == irace == The output of targetRunner must be one number 'cost'!
== irace == The call to targetRunner was:
/home/mohamedey/hyperedattp/target-runner 1 33 509998482 33   ns=3 Nsmp=7 Nsurv=3 N=26 sr=4 sel=1
== irace == The output was:

== irace == This is not a bug in irace, but means that something failed when running the command(s) above or they were terminated before completion. Try to run the command(s) above from the execution directory '/home/mohamedey/hyperedattp' to investigate the issue.

However, when I use only one core it seems to work fine.

By the way, when I execute the command
/home/mohamedey/hyperedattp/target-runner 1 33 509998482 33 ns=3 Nsmp=7 Nsurv=3 N=26 sr=4 sel=1
and it worked without a problem as well.

Any ideas how to solve this issue ?

Thank you !
--
Mohamed

messages.subject: Re: irace issue with parallel cores
messages.body_plain:
On Monday, 31 October 2016 11:31:44 UTC, Mohamed El Yafrani wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I'm having a hard time running EDA in parallel on a university server. When I tried to use 10, 16, and 3 cores (by setting parallel to N in scenario.txt), I got the following error (repeated several times):
>

> Any ideas how to solve this issue ?

Dear Mohamed,

There may be a bug in irace, but usually when one gets the above error, there is some problem in target-runner. A few things worth checking:

* Does 'only one core' mean that you run with parallel=1 on the same machine that gives the error with parallel=2? The key here is 'on the same machine'. If you need to submit jobs through a queuing system, the running environment when using the queuing system may not be the same as when you launch irace yourself. The queuing system may also send the job to different machines depending on the number of CPUs requested.

* Does target-runner read/create intermediate files? Can these files cause a race condition when two calls to target-runner happen at the same time? Maybe these files consume too much memory or fill the filesystem when there are simultaneous target-runner calls?

* Does your university server impose any limits on number of processes, CPU/memory/filesystem use per job? Such limits may kill the target-runner process before it has a chance to print anything useful and irace cannot detect what the problem is.

You could try to create a dummy target-runner that only prints what you expect to be printed by the actual target-runner without executing any other program or reading/writing any files, and see if that works.

Manuel.
